Do not start any work yet. I want to work through a few features that you can do and hash out all of the details, and once we have done that, you are to implement them. So the first thing that I think of is that we still need to make a selection toolbar. This toolbar can be just like the save and edit toolbars, with those in the top toolbar, although it would only show when in design mode. The first can be a drop down box for a single curve, connected curves, or tangent curves. and the second drop-down box would be the selection filter, where when it's dropped down, it is checkboxes for things like planes, bodies, surfaces, curves and points. 

What other features can we outline and fully define right now

For the purposes of the selection toolbar, I would say that surfaces are sheets not associated with bodies, and faces are their own category in which must be associated with a body. Edges must also be associated with a body. Curves are specifically drawing items, whether it's a 2D curve on a sketch or a 3D curve in space, like an isocline. However, I would say that the same goes for points. A point would be in a sketch, or it can also be the origin. However, a vertex would be the corners on a body. Other selection options, I think the biggest one is dragging left to right and right to left. In the toolbar, you can have a button that enables and disables directional selection. I would also say that there should be a toggle button for persistent selection. What I mean by this is that if you select three curves and make them all equal length by adding the equal constraint, the program does not immediately clear the selection. With persistent selection toggled on, it keeps those three lines highlighted so that the user can then additionally do something like make all three construction geometry at once.

Directional selection and persistent selection should both default to on. For the single connected tangent curves, I guess it can apply to both drawing curves and body edges. Escape and clicking empty space should deselect all items, even when persistent selection is turned on. Otherwise, use all suggestions that you had for these items that you had suggested earlier. Do not use or implement any of the other selection features that you had suggested at this time. Still don't do anything yet. Let's move on to the next feature to fully define.
Does FreeCAD implement layers?

Yes, I want to implement a layer system for the design mode. We can have a toolbar for it in the top toolbar as well that only shows in design mode. Clicking the Layers button will open the Layers task panel. We should have a default work layer in which the origin must always reside, and then all other items within the model history should be able to be moved from one layer to another.

With regard to your suggestions, I would say that something like the work layer should be renamed to something like the base layer, because one of the first things I forgot to mention is that we should be able to make it so that the user is able to switch between layers, making one layer active or another, and while that layer is active, all things that they do are attributed immediately to that layer. So I would scratch your new items start on work layer, or if we're going to call it the base layer, unless the user is currently working on a different layer. The task panel should support all of those features, and deleting a layer should move geometry back to the base layer. It should not be able to delete geometry, and they should be saved with the document and support undo redo. There should be an eye next to the layers in the task panel to toggle visibility. It should also be able to double-click a layer to make it active, and then likely signify that that layer is active by making the text bold, and maybe a check mark next to it to indicate that it is active. And when it comes to sketch contents and just whole items in general, I feel like a whole sketch should be required to be assigned to a single layer, and I also feel like bodies should be assigned to a single layer, not able to be separated by a single body created by a loft, a revolve, and a subtract extrude. Those all end up in creating a single body, and therefore it would not make sense to try to separate them out to different layers.

Your rule does not fully capture my intent. My thought is that a single object cannot be split between multiple layers. So a sketch is a single object, and thus the curves within a sketch should not be able to be separated between multiple layers. A sketch and a body are two separate objects. So even if a sketch is used to create a body, that sketch can still remain on a different layer than the body. However, if a single body is made by multiple operations, such as extrude and revolve, what's really being assigned to the layer is the body, not the operations that created that single object body. Therefore, by default, all of the operations to correct the body must reside on a single layer. We should also add that the top toolbar can have more buttons on it. We could have a button for Move to Layer, in which all pre-selected items would then be moved to a layer chosen as a drop-down of that button. Similar, there could be a Change Active Layer button that doesn't work like a traditional button in that pressing the button opens a drop-down of which layer to select yet again. I don't know if that is making sense, but I think it's a way to have a drop-down box without having the normal wide box with the current value. It would just be a button that drops down all of the options to be selected.
What other extremely high utility features were outlined in the development roadmap?

Here are the items that I want to set in the current workload queue: the contextual constraint palette, the precise move, copy, and movable pivot workflow, the sketch freedom and constraint repair, interactive feature handles, and broken reference repair. Start with the first one and ask any questions that you need until we've fully defined and outlined.

I suggest having it appear when an object is clicked. However, it can be relatively easy to make disappear, either by moving the pointer away from the palette box, or just a simple five-second timeout. It should only contain constraints and the construction geometry toggle, as well as driving and reference dimension toggles.

I would say that the timer should actually be one second if it travels outside of a small travel corridor. I would also say that the palette should appear above the pointer. And so the workflow would be click a geometry, constraint palette shows above the pointer. The user can then choose something on the palette, or if they move outside of the travel corridor, it quickly disappears within one second. That allows the user to be able to move the mouse, and if they don't move it perfectly directly towards the palette, it stays visible with a very short grace period. But if they move outside of that corridor, it also disappears very quickly. I would also say that multiple selections should indeed update the palette for the entire current selection, and it should indeed restart the timer. With persistent selection turned on, the palette should also stay visible until the user leaves the travel corridor. If persistent selection is turned off, then of course as soon as the constraint is applied, there would be nothing selected anymore for the palette to refer to, and thus it should disappear. Conflicting or existing constraints should simply be grayed out with a tool tip upon hover, and constraints that do not apply to the selected geometry types should not be visible.

If the pointer is too close to the boundary of the viewport, you may move it to wherever is needed to stay within the viewport. So even if it's supposed to be above the pointer, but the pointer is in the top right-hand corner of the viewport, the palette can be shown to the bottom left of it. With the mix of construction geometry, I would say that the first click should make all curves normal, and a second click makes them all construction. When dimensions are selected, you can have two buttons on the palette, one for make driving and one for make reference. It can support multiple all at one time, and if it causes a conflict and an invalid sketch, it can just throw that error.
With regard to if make driving produces an invalid sketch, I would say just keep it as invalid and the user can either click undo, or they can troubleshoot it one dimension at a time.

The move feature should only refer to whole components, which would include all of its child components as well. If the user is doing a copy, this would just be another instance of that component, in which we have already defined that all instances in the part tree are merely linked copies of the components in the model tab. All moves should be one task panel and always open in the task panel. From there, there should be several workflows depending upon the first drop-down box, also the first field in the panel, which can be translate, rotate, point-to-point, align axes, align coordinate systems, or interactive, or something like the word interactive, in which the user uses handles to push and pull or rotate the object manually.

I would actually say that creating a copy causes issues here. If a user wants to create a copy, they can do a copy and paste in the part tree, and then move it afterwards. Otherwise placement in the part tree does become difficult. Thus the buttons can then easily be... actually I take it back. Since moves can often be a series of translates and rotations, I would say that Apply, OK, and Cancel should all be available, where OK applies and closes the box, or the panel, task panel, whereas Apply, of course, applies that move but leaves the task panel open with the same selected components. In addition, I would say that even before, or maybe you can put it after the movement type drop-down box, have a list box for all the components to be moved, so that the user can move multiple components at once. And again, it is not necessary for a user to select a component and its child. Once a user selects a component, only that component is recorded in the list box, and all of its children are automatically included.

Translate should always be a vector and a distance. The vector can be local axes, global axes, or something like an edge or a line. It should also have a reverse button just in case the direction was opposite of desired.

I would say we should actually do away with the local axes. I think since a part or component belongs to the next higher assembly, moving a part should always be with respect to the next higher part. And so if the user clicks a component, it should immediately make the next higher assembly the active component. And from that point on, the user can only select other components or sibling components within that parent. After apply, I would say that the components can still remain highlighted if persistent selection is turned on. However, the direction, the reverse state, and the distance should all be reset.

Before we go there, do you get what I mean by the parent owns the location of a component within its assembly? Because if you open that component in its own window, the parent component, that is, the child component isn't measured with regard to its location to the top-level assembly. A component is always located based upon its parent. And so editing one component within a parent will move the component within all instances of the top-level assembly, which could cause, which would most likely cause adverse effects. And so the components selected must always be under a single parent, and the movement is in relation to the parent coordinate system, always. With regard to rotate, persistent selection off should also apply the empty component list after applying a rotation. For both this, by this I mean rotate and translate, any visible geometry may be utilized for the vector or axis of rotation. However, the resulting location and orientation is again recorded with respect to its parent, not the global coordinate system. And yes, only siblings may be moved, multiple at one time, within an active parent.
Is this now done for movement? What feature groups have we completed? What feature groups still need to be defined and outlined?

I need to go to sleep, so I want you to create a queue of prompts, making it as many prompts as needed, especially for the Move Components. You are to make the prompts to implement the Selection Toolbar, the Layers implementation and its toolbar, and Contextual Constraint Palette. You are to also implement the Move Components, utilize the outlines that I have already given to you, and extrapolate to determine what to do for the other workflows within the Move Components workflow only. Leave the other queued items, including Sketch Freedom and Constraint Repair, Interactive Feature Handles, and Broken Reference Repair for later. We will outline and define them before you work them. So again, you are going to create a series of prompts, one or more prompt per feature group, enter them into the queue, and then work them sequentially to completion for the Selection Toolbar, Layers, Context Constraint Palette, and Move Components.

Do not create a duplicate status roadmap. Batch costly native rebuild and packaged acceptance across these related prompts, with explicit deferred validation for prompt 10. Do not call source-prepared work owner-ready. Do not stop at a plan or stub. Do not ask the sleeping owner to repeat settled decisions. Use routine implementation judgment without adding new product scope.

Create a top toolbar alongside the Save and Edit toolbars, visible only in Design mode. The first control is a dropdown labeled by selection intent with Single Curve, Connected Curves, Tangent Curves; apply these modes to both drawing curves and body edges. Default to Single Curve. Reuse native connectivity/tangency handling where appropriate; define deterministic branch, loop, shared endpoint and tolerance behavior in the canonical requirements and test it, without silently crossing independent sketches/bodies or treating screen overlap as geometric connection. Do not introduce extra selection modes.

The second control is a checkbox filter dropdown with Planes, Bodies, Surfaces, Faces, Edges, Curves, Points, Vertices. Independent enabled categories form the eligible selection set, intersected with current command input gates. Planes are reference planes; Bodies are whole bodies; Surfaces are sheets not associated with bodies; Faces belong to bodies; Edges belong to bodies; Curves are drawing items, including sketch curves and standalone 3D curves such as isoclines; Points are sketch points, standalone reference points and origins; Vertices are body corners/vertices. Do not classify every TopoDS edge as a body Edge or every face as a body Face. Preserve occurrence identity when resolving selected objects. Category filters must work with native clicking, preselection and directional box selection, and not break task-specific reference collectors.

Add Directional Selection and Persistent Selection toggle buttons, both ON by default and remembering the user's choices between sessions. Directional ON: left-to-right box selection requires full enclosure; right-to-left also includes intersected items. OFF: both directions require full enclosure. Give enclosure and crossing rectangles distinct appearance and honor filters in both modes. Persistent ON: successful operations retain surviving selected entities for successive actions, e.g. select three lines, apply Equal, then make them Construction without reselecting. Failed operations retain selection; deleted items leave selection. Persistent OFF follows normal post-operation clearing. Escape and clicking empty space deselect everything even when Persistent is ON. Ordinary selection replacement/addition still behaves normally. Use a shared policy that the upcoming constraint palette and Move task can consume; do not implement persistence by indiscriminately restoring stale subelement indices or overriding active collector ownership.

Acceptance: verify toolbar Design-only lifecycle including switching modes, saved toggle defaults/settings, entity taxonomy, native filter intersections, left/right directional behavior, connected/tangent selection, Equal then Construction with persistent selection, deletion/failure cleanup, Escape/empty click, undo/redo, and no command-gate regression. Carry native runtime/build checks requiring a grouped rebuild to prompt 10 explicitly. Continue through implementation and documentation; the next native queued prompt is Layers. The .txt files in this folder are prompt backups, not an instruction to enqueue or execute duplicates.

Every document has a permanent layer named Base. It cannot be deleted or renamed. Origin objects always reside on Base and cannot be reassigned. Exactly one layer is active, initially Base. New independent objects immediately receive the active layer. All other eligible Model History objects can move between layers subject to the indivisible-object rule below. Each object has exactly one layer assignment. Layers and assignments are document data, saved/reopened in supported native documents and undoable/redoable, including active-layer changes. Migration of existing documents assigns previously unassigned eligible objects to Base without destructive replacement.

A sketch is one object: all its curves/points remain together. A body is one object: its body-building operations follow its layer; do not put successive extrude/revolve/subtract operations for the same body on separate layers. A sketch and the body consuming it are SEPARATE objects and can reside on different layers, even when native ownership nests the sketch under a Body. Moving the body must NOT move its input sketches. Selecting a body operation for reassignment resolves to the owning body; selecting a sketch moves that sketch only. New operations on an existing body retain the body's layer without reassigning independent input sketches. Do not let a broad native container recursion swallow this explicit distinction.

Add a Layers top toolbar alongside existing toolbars, visible only in Design mode. It contains Layers, Move to Layer (compact menu button), and Change Active Layer (compact menu button). These are fixed-label buttons opening a dropdown on the whole button, not wide current-value combo boxes and not split default-action buttons. Layers opens the Layers task panel. Move to Layer lists document layers and moves preselected eligible objects to the chosen layer in one transaction; disable when no eligible selection exists, preserve the fixed Origin rule and deduplicate bodies resolved from multiple operations. Change Active Layer lists layers and marks the active one with a check. It changes the layer for subsequently created independent objects.

The task panel supports creating, renaming, deleting, assigning objects and choosing the active layer. Double-click a layer to activate it; show its name bold plus a check mark. Each row has an eye visibility control. Hide gates layer members' visibility without destroying their individual visibility states; showing restores those states and must not expose historical intermediate body results. Keep sketches on other layers independently visible/hidden. Avoid recompute or dependency changes from visibility alone. Deleting any non-Base layer moves its objects to Base and NEVER deletes geometry. Deleting the active layer activates Base. Preserve object-level visibility semantics and explicit individual visibility changes while hidden without destructive snapshots.

Acceptance must cover Base/origin protection, active creation, independent sketch/body assignment, operation-to-body resolution, multi-object reassignment, layer deletion with geometry unchanged, active fallback, native undo/redo, save/reopen including .cadprt where supported, old-document initialization, visibility restoration without intermediate-result leakage, repeated component contexts, task/toolbar lifecycle and saved data integrity. Record runtime checks deferred to the final grouped build. Continue to a working implementation; prompt 3 then implements the constraint palette. Backups here must not be reenqueued.

Implement the fully specified Contextual Constraint Palette in FreeCAD Plus. This is prompt 3 of 10 in the authorized sequential workload, after Selection and Layers. Reuse and repair prerequisites as necessary. The owner authorizes implementation now; the earlier planning hold no longer applies to these four feature groups. Keep Sketch Freedom and Constraint Repair, Interactive Feature Handles, Broken Reference Repair and other selection features deferred. Reporting native solver errors is required here but does not authorize building the separate repair feature.

Follow PROGRAMMING_SUMMARY and current applicable project/central/workspace instructions. Inspect and reuse native Sketcher constraints, selection and solver services. Preserve current changes and constraint/document identities. Implement real behavior and meaningful quick regression checks. Update canonical roadmap/WORK_STATE, interaction requirements, and the owner DOCX using the Documents skill; preserve owner edits, headings and automatic numbering and render/verify changed pages. Batch expensive native build/packaged checks into prompt 10 and report deferred verification honestly. Do not end at a mocked palette or duplicate solver.

While editing a sketch, clicking geometry opens the palette above the pointer and bases its actions on the ENTIRE current selection. Additional selection clicks update that selection/action set and reset dismissal timing. Box selection alone does not open it. Prefer above the click, but reposition in any direction, including bottom-left near the top-right corner, to keep the full palette inside the sketch viewport. Maintain a small usable travel corridor from the triggering pointer position to the actual palette rectangle. While inside the palette or corridor, it stays visible indefinitely. Leaving the combined region starts a one-second timer; reentering cancels it. Do not use the earlier five-second suggestion or a fixed timeout while inside. Layout must remain usable with narrow views and high DPI without jumping under the pointer during action updates. Dismissing it by pointer travel does not clear selection.

Only show applicable constraints, Construction Geometry, and Make Driving/Make Reference. Hide structurally inapplicable constraints. Existing, redundant and known-conflicting constraint actions are greyed out with hover explanations; the tooltip must work on disabled actions. Hover may highlight affected geometry but never applies or adds a constraint. Revalidate actions against the current sketch/selection before execution; unknown solver feasibility is not automatically a known conflict. Use native eligibility/solver checks without mutating the committed sketch merely for preview.

Construction conversion: a mixed normal/construction curve selection becomes ALL NORMAL on the first toggle, then ALL CONSTRUCTION on the next. Uniform all-normal selections become all-construction and uniform all-construction become all-normal. Do not confuse reference dimensions with construction geometry.

For selected dimensions, provide two separate buttons, Make Driving and Make Reference; both support multiple dimensions as one undoable action. Explicit owner exception: allow Make Driving to be attempted even when it results in a solver conflict/invalid sketch. Keep the converted state and display the native solver error, so the user may Undo the entire batch or troubleshoot dimensions individually. Do not silently roll back or delete constraints to obtain a valid result. Preserve dimension values, identities, expressions, existing relationships and native unsupported-operation safeguards; distinguish a committed invalid solve from an API/input failure. Other known-conflicting constraint additions stay disabled as specified.

Persistent Selection ON: retain surviving selected geometry/dimensions after an action, keep the palette visible until the pointer leaves its travel region, and update actions in place. OFF: successfully applied actions clear the selection and close the palette. Escape and empty-space clicking clear selection and close the palette. Clean up timers/observers/highlight on sketch exit, document close, task transitions and deletion. Failed uncommitted actions preserve selection; committed invalid Make Driving remains undoable and reports its error.

Acceptance: actual pointer/click corridor behavior and one-second cancellation, viewport edge repositioning, multiselection updates, disabled-action tooltips, no mutation on hover, Equal then Construction, mixed conversion normal-first, multiple driving/reference conversion, intentionally invalid committed driving conversion with Undo, persistent on/off, Escape/empty click, undo/redo and save/reopen. Record any checks awaiting prompt 10's grouped native runtime. Implement completely before proceeding to the Move Components sequence; do not enqueue copies of these backup prompts.

Move acts only on whole COMPONENT INSTANCES in the Part Tree, including their descendants. Component definitions live in Models; Part Tree instances are linked copies. Copying is done through existing Part Tree copy/paste, outside this command. Do not duplicate shapes, create independent definitions, add Copy controls or change ownership while moving.

CRITICAL OWNERSHIP: a parent component DEFINITION owns each child instance's relative placement within it. Selecting the first movable instance activates its immediate parent assembly as the edit context. Subsequently accept only siblings directly under that same parent. A child is stored relative to its parent, never to top-level/world coordinates. Editing a child in shared parent A changes the corresponding child in every occurrence of A. Do not create a display-occurrence-only placement override. A top-level/root without a movable parent must be handled explicitly using the project's root/master contract, not guessed as a freely movable global object. Maintain the exact selected occurrence path for converting displayed references when parent definitions appear multiple times. Verify this by opening the parent independently and by rendering multiple differently transformed occurrences of it.

Always open one TASK PANEL, not a modal standalone dialog. First field: workflow dropdown in exact order Translate, Rotate, Point to Point, Align Axes, Align Coordinate Systems, Interactive. Next: component selection list with add/remove/clear through existing collector conventions. Each listed parent carries all its descendants implicitly; no expanded child list and no double transform. First eligible preselection establishes context; reject incompatible cross-parent selections with inline explanation instead of moving a partial unexpected set. Several siblings move as one rigid group with their relative placements preserved. Do not hijack ordinary component clicks outside the Move task to activate parents.

Provide Apply, OK, Cancel. Preview is transient and clearly shows intended placements without committing document mutations. Apply commits all selected siblings atomically as one undoable action, keeps the panel open and resets all movement inputs. OK applies any valid nonzero pending movement and closes; after Apply, OK simply closes instead of reapplying. Cancel discards current preview, closes and keeps already-applied transactions available through Undo. Persistent Selection ON retains the list/highlights; OFF clears both after Apply. Workflow changes discard only uncommitted movement parameters/preview while preserving eligible selected siblings and active parent. No-op Apply must not create undo records. Errors leave a recoverable panel. Respect existing constrained/driven/read-only instance guards; do not silently break assembly joints.

Translate is ALWAYS one normalized direction vector plus a nonnegative length Distance and a Reverse button. Direction choices: active PARENT X/Y/Z or picked straight edge, line/reference axis from ANY visible geometry. No global-vs-local dropdown and no independent per-child frames or XYZ displacement triplets. Convert picked world/occurrence direction into active-parent coordinates; distinguish direction vectors from positions so parent translation does not affect the vector. Reject zero/undefined or unsuitable curved references clearly. Snapshot references for a placement operation, not new associative model dependencies. Reverse flips the direction, retaining distance. All siblings use the same parent-frame vector and distance. After Apply: direction unset, Reverse OFF, Distance zero; parent context remains for a series of moves.

Build the reusable transform/reference/preview/commit machinery for the actual upcoming six workflows without speculative unrelated frameworks. Remaining workflow entries may be identified as awaiting their next queued implementation, but do not claim those methods complete. Acceptance: nested rotated parents, shared parent occurrences and standalone-parent opening, siblings only, implicit descendants, correct frame conversions using any visible reference, unchanged source definitions/geometry, group relative transforms, reverse/distance, Apply-then-OK, Cancel after Apply, persistent on/off, atomic undo/redo and save/reopen. Later prompts must finish all six workflows before owner delivery. Do not reenqueue backup files.

Keep the mandatory owner contract: only whole sibling component instances under a single active immediate parent; children follow implicitly; parent definitions own child relative placements so shared parent occurrences all reflect edits.
